verses.1:1: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD from the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying,
verses.1:2: "Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given to me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has charged me to build for Him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
verses.1:3: Who among you is of all His people? Let his God be with him, and let him ascend to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel—He is the God who is in Jerusalem.
verses.1:4: And as for everyone who remains, in any of the places where he sojourns, let the men of his place support him with silver and with gold, with goods and with livestock, together with the freewill offering for the house of God which is in Jerusalem."
verses.1:5: Then the heads of the fathers' houses of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests and the Levites, arose—everyone whose spirit God had stirred up—to go up to build the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem.
verses.1:6: And all who were around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, with livestock, and with choice gifts, besides all that was freely offered.
verses.1:7: King Cyrus also brought forth the vessels of the house of the LORD, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought out from Jerusalem and placed in the house of his gods.
verses.1:8: Cyrus king of Persia brought them forth by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and numbered them to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.
verses.1:9: And this was their number: thirty basins of gold, one thousand basins of silver, twenty-nine knives;
verses.1:10: thirty bowls of gold, four hundred and ten bowls of silver of a second sort, and one thousand other vessels.
verses.1:11: All the vessels of gold and of silver were five thousand four hundred. All of these Sheshbazzar brought up when the exiles were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.
verses.2:1: And these are the sons of the province who went up from the captivity of the exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away to Babylon, and who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each man to his own city.
verses.2:2: They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
verses.2:3: The sons of Parosh: two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
verses.2:4: The sons of Shephatiah: three hundred seventy-two.
verses.2:5: The sons of Arah: seven hundred seventy-five.
verses.2:6: The sons of Pahath-Moab, of the sons of Jeshua and Joab: two thousand eight hundred twelve.
verses.2:7: The sons of Elam: one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
verses.2:8: The sons of Zattu: nine hundred forty-five.
verses.2:9: The sons of Zaccai: seven hundred sixty.
verses.2:10: The sons of Bani: six hundred forty-two.
verses.2:11: The sons of Bebai: six hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:12: The sons of Azgad: one thousand two hundred twenty-two.
verses.2:13: The sons of Adonikam: six hundred sixty-six.
verses.2:14: The sons of Bigvai: two thousand fifty-six.
verses.2:15: The sons of Adin: four hundred fifty-four.
verses.2:16: The sons of Ater, of Hezekiah: ninety-eight.
verses.2:17: The sons of Bezai: three hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:18: The sons of Jorah: one hundred twelve.
verses.2:19: The sons of Hashum: two hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:21: The sons of Bethlehem: one hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:23: The men of Anathoth: one hundred twenty-eight.
verses.2:25: The sons of Kiriath Arim, Chephirah, and Beeroth: seven hundred forty-three.
verses.2:26: The sons of Ramah and Geba: six hundred twenty-one.
verses.2:27: The men of Michmas: one hundred twenty-two.
verses.2:28: The men of Bethel and Ai: two hundred twenty-three.
verses.2:30: The sons of Magbish: one hundred fifty-six.
verses.2:31: The sons of the other Elam: one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
verses.2:32: The sons of Harim: three hundred twenty.
verses.2:33: The sons of Lod, Hadid, and Ono: seven hundred twenty-five.
verses.2:34: The sons of Jericho: three hundred forty-five.
verses.2:35: The sons of Senaah: three thousand six hundred thirty.
verses.2:36: The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred seventy-three.
verses.2:37: The sons of Immer: one thousand fifty-two.
verses.2:38: The sons of Pashhur: one thousand two hundred forty-seven.
verses.2:39: The sons of Harim: one thousand seventeen.
verses.2:40: The Levites: the sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodaviah, seventy-four.
verses.2:41: The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred twenty-eight.
verses.2:42: The sons of the gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, and the sons of Shobai—in all, one hundred thirty-nine.
verses.2:43: The temple servants: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth;
verses.2:44: the sons of Keros, the sons of Siaha, the sons of Padon;
verses.2:45: the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Akkub;
verses.2:46: the sons of Hagab, the sons of Shalmai, the sons of Hanan;
verses.2:47: the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar, the sons of Reaiah;
verses.2:48: the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda, the sons of Gazzam;
verses.2:49: the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah, the sons of Besai;
verses.2:50: the sons of Asnah, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Nephusim;
verses.2:51: the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur;
verses.2:52: the sons of Bazluth, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha;
verses.2:53: the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah;
verses.2:54: the sons of Neziah, and the sons of Hatipha.
verses.2:55: The sons of Solomon's servants: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Hassophereth, the sons of Peruda;
verses.2:56: the sons of Jaalah, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel;
verses.2:57: the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-Hazzebaim, and the sons of Ami.
verses.2:58: All the temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants were three hundred ninety-two.
verses.2:59: And these were those who went up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer, yet they were not able to declare their fathers' house or their descent, whether they were of Israel:
verses.2:60: the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, and the sons of Nekoda: six hundred fifty-two.
verses.2:61: And of the sons of the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, and the sons of Barzillai, who had taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
verses.2:62: These sought their written record among those enrolled by genealogy, but they were not found; therefore they were excluded as defiled from the priesthood.
verses.2:63: And the governor told them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest arose with Urim and Thummim.
verses.2:64: The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
verses.2:65: besides their male and female servants, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven; and they had two hundred singing men and singing women.
verses.2:66: Their horses were seven hundred thirty-six; their mules were two hundred forty-five.
verses.2:67: Their camels were four hundred thirty-five; and donkeys, six thousand seven hundred twenty.
verses.2:68: And some of the heads of the fathers' houses, when they came to the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem, made freewill offerings for the house of God, to erect it upon its site.
verses.2:69: According to their ability, they gave to the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priests' garments.
verses.2:70: So the priests and the Levites, along with some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants, dwelt in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.
verses.3:1: When the seventh month arrived, and the children of Israel were in the cities, the people assembled as one man to Jerusalem.
verses.3:2: Then Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brethren the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brethren, arose and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings upon it, as is written in the Law of Moses the man of God.
verses.3:3: And they set the altar firmly upon its bases, for dread was upon them because of the peoples of the lands; and they offered burnt offerings upon it to the LORD, burnt offerings for the morning and for the evening.
verses.3:4: They also observed the Feast of Tabernacles as is written, with the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the ordinance for the requirement of each day.
verses.3:5: And afterward they offered the continual burnt offering, both for the New Moons and for all the consecrated appointed feasts of the LORD, as well as for everyone who willingly brought a freewill offering to the LORD.
verses.3:6: From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, though the foundation of the temple of the LORD had not yet been laid.
verses.3:7: They also gave silver to the stonecutters and the craftsmen, and food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and the Tyrians, to bring cedar timbers from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, according to the grant of Cyrus king of Persia to them.
verses.3:8: Now in the second year after their coming to the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, with the rest of their brethren the priests and the Levites, and all who had returned from the captivity to Jerusalem, began the work and appointed the Levites from twenty years old and upward to oversee the work of the house of the LORD.
verses.3:9: Then Jeshua, with his sons and his brethren, and Kadmiel with his sons, the sons of Judah, stood together as one to oversee those performing the work in the house of God, along with the sons of Henadad, their sons, and their brethren the Levites.
verses.3:10: When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, they stationed the priests in their vestments with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the ordinance of David king of Israel.
verses.3:11: And they sang responsively, praising and giving thanks to the LORD: "For He is good, for His lovingkindness endures forever toward Israel." And all the people raised a great shout in praising the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid.
verses.3:12: Yet many of the priests and Levites and heads of the fathers' houses, aged men who had seen the first house, wept with a loud voice when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, while many lifted up their voice with a shout of joy.
verses.3:13: So the people could not distinguish the sound of the shout of joy from the sound of the weeping of the people, for the people shouted with a great shout, and the sound was heard far away.
verses.4:1: Now the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity were building a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.4:2: And they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the fathers' houses and said to them, "Let us build with you, for we seek your God as you do; and to Him we have been sacrificing since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here."
verses.4:3: But Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the rest of the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel said to them, "It is not for you and us together to build a house for our God, but we alone will build for the LORD, the God of Israel, just as King Cyrus, the king of Persia, has commanded us."
verses.4:4: Then the people of the land kept weakening the hands of the people of Judah and frightening them from building.
verses.4:5: They also hired counselors against them to frustrate their purpose all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
verses.4:6: And in the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.4:7: And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia; and the writing of the letter was written in Aramaic and translated into Aramaic.
verses.4:8: Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes in this manner:
verses.4:9: Then Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates—the Dinaites, the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Shushanchites, the Dehaites, the Elamites,
verses.4:10: and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar deported and settled in the city of Samaria and the rest of the region Beyond the River—and so forth.
verses.4:11: This is a copy of the letter that they sent to him: "To King Artaxerxes: Your servants, the men of the region Beyond the River. And now,
verses.4:12: Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from you have come to us at Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city, finishing the walls, and repairing the foundations.
verses.4:13: Now let it be known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, they will not pay tribute, custom, or toll, and it will bring loss to the treasury of the kings.
verses.4:14: Now because we eat the salt of the palace, and it is not fitting for us to witness the king's dishonor, therefore we have sent and informed the king,
verses.4:15: that search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. You will find in the book of the records and know that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that they have stirred up sedition within it from days of old; for this reason this city was laid waste.
verses.4:16: We inform the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, by this means you will have no portion in the region Beyond the River."
verses.4:17: Then the king sent an answer: "To Rehum the commander, to Shimshai the scribe, to the rest of their associates who dwell in Samaria, and to the rest of the region Beyond the River: Peace. And now,
verses.4:18: The letter which you sent to us has been plainly read before me.
verses.4:19: And a decree was issued by me, and search was made, and it has been found that this city from days of old has risen up against kings, and that rebellion and sedition have been committed in it.
verses.4:20: Mighty kings have also ruled over Jerusalem, exercising dominion over all the region Beyond the River; and tribute, custom, and toll were paid to them.
verses.4:21: Now issue a decree to make those men cease, that this city shall not be rebuilt until a decree is issued by me.
verses.4:22: And take heed not to be negligent in carrying out this matter. Why should harm increase to the detriment of the kings?"
verses.4:23: Then, as soon as the copy of the letter of King Artaxerxes was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, they went in haste to Jerusalem against the Jews, and by force and power made them cease.
verses.4:24: Thus the work of the house of God which is at Jerusalem ceased, and it remained halted until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
verses.5:1: Then Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo, the prophets, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.
verses.5:2: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak arose and began to build the house of God which is at Jerusalem; and the prophets of God were with them, supporting them.
verses.5:3: At that same time Tattenai, governor of the region Beyond the River, and Shethar-Boznai and their associates came to them and spoke thus to them: "Who issued you a decree to build this house and to finish this structure?"
verses.5:4: Then accordingly we told them what the names of the men were who were constructing this building.
verses.5:5: But the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, so that they did not make them cease until the report should go to Darius, and then a written reply should be returned concerning this matter.
verses.5:6: This is a copy of the letter that Tattenai, governor of the region Beyond the River, and Shethar-Boznai and his associates, the Apharsachites who were in the region Beyond the River, sent to King Darius.
verses.5:7: They sent a report to him, and in it was written thus: "To King Darius: All peace.
verses.5:8: Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God, which is being built with huge stones, and timber is being laid in the walls; and this work is being carried out diligently and prospers in their hands.
verses.5:9: Then we questioned those elders and spoke to them in this manner: 'Who issued you a decree to build this house and to finish this structure?'
verses.5:10: We also asked them their names to inform you, that we might write down the names of the men who were at their head.
verses.5:11: And thus they returned us an answer, saying: 'We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the house that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and finished.
verses.5:12: But because our fathers provoked the God of heaven to wrath, He gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house and carried the people away into exile in Babylon.
verses.5:13: However, in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued a decree to rebuild this house of God.
verses.5:14: And also the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple that was in Jerusalem and brought into the temple of Babylon, those King Cyrus took out of the temple of Babylon, and they were delivered to one whose name was Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor.
verses.5:15: And he said to him, "Take these vessels, go, deposit them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt on its site."
verses.5:16: Then this same Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God which is in Jerusalem; and from that time even until now it has been under construction, and it is not yet finished.'
verses.5:17: Now therefore, if it seems good to the king, let search be made in the royal treasure house there in Babylon, to see whether a decree was issued by King Cyrus to rebuild this house of God in Jerusalem; and let the king send us his pleasure concerning this matter."
verses.6:1: Then King Darius issued a decree, and a search was made in the house of the archives, where the treasures were stored in Babylon.
verses.6:2: And in Ecbatana, in the citadel that is in the province of Media, a scroll was found, and within it a record was written thus:
verses.6:3: "In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus issued a decree concerning the house of God in Jerusalem: Let the house be rebuilt, the place where they offer sacrifices, and let its foundations be firmly laid; its height shall be sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits,
verses.6:4: with three courses of heavy stones and a course of new timber; and let the cost be paid from the king's treasury.
verses.6:5: And also let the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple that is in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, be restored and returned to the temple that is in Jerusalem, each to its place, and you shall deposit them in the house of God."
verses.6:6: "Now therefore, Tattenai, governor of the region beyond the River, Shethar-Boznai, and your companions, the officials who are beyond the River, keep far away from there.
verses.6:7: Leave the work on this house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God on its site.
verses.6:8: Moreover, I issue a decree regarding what you shall do for these elders of the Jews for the rebuilding of this house of God: from the king's resources, out of the tribute of the region beyond the River, the expenses shall be paid in full to these men without interruption.
verses.6:9: And whatever is needed—young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and oil—according to the word of the priests who are in Jerusalem, let it be given to them day by day without fail,
verses.6:10: that they may offer sacrifices of sweet aroma to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
verses.6:11: Also I issue a decree that if any man alters this edict, let a beam be pulled out from his house, and let him be lifted up and impaled upon it, and let his house be made a refuse heap because of this.
verses.6:12: And may the God who has caused His name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who puts forth his hand to alter or to destroy this house of God that is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued a decree; let it be carried out with all diligence."
verses.6:13: Then Tattenai, governor of the region beyond the River, Shethar-Boznai, and their companions did with all diligence according to what King Darius had sent.
verses.6:14: So the elders of the Jews built and prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. And they built and finished it, according to the command of the God of Israel and according to the decree of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
verses.6:15: Now this house was finished on the third day of the month of Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
verses.6:16: Then the children of Israel, the priests and the Levites and the rest of the children of the captivity, celebrated the dedication of this house of God with joy.
verses.6:17: And they offered at the dedication of this house of God one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and as a sin offering for all Israel twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
verses.6:18: They appointed the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their courses for the service of God in Jerusalem, as it is written in the Book of Moses.
verses.6:19: And the children of the captivity kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.6:20: For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves together; all of them were ceremonially clean. So they slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the children of the captivity, for their brethren the priests, and for themselves.
verses.6:21: Then the children of Israel who had returned from the captivity ate it, together with all who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the nations of the land to join them in seeking the LORD God of Israel.
verses.6:22: And they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with joy; for the LORD made them joyful, and turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God, the God of Israel.
verses.7:1: Now after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra the son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,
verses.7:2: the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,
verses.7:3: the son of Amariah, the son of Azariah, the son of Meraioth,
verses.7:4: the son of Zerahiah, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,
verses.7:5: the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest—
verses.7:6: this Ezra came up from Babylon; and he was a skilled scribe in the Law of Moses, which the LORD God of Israel had given. And the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of the LORD his God upon him.
verses.7:7: Some of the children of Israel, and some of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the Nethinim went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
verses.7:8: And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king.
verses.7:9: For on the first day of the first month he began the journey up from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God upon him.
verses.7:10: For Ezra had steadfastly set his heart to search the Law of the LORD, and to practice it, and to teach statute and ordinance in Israel.
verses.7:11: Now this is the copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe—a scribe of the words of the commandments of the LORD and of His statutes for Israel:
verses.7:12: "Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of heaven: All peace, and now.
verses.7:13: I issue a decree that any of the people of Israel in my kingdom, and their priests and the Levites, who freely volunteers to go to Jerusalem, may go with you.
verses.7:14: Because you are sent by the king and his seven counselors to inquire concerning Judah and Jerusalem according to the law of your God, which is in your hand,
verses.7:15: and to carry the silver and gold which the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,
verses.7:16: along with all the silver and gold that you shall find in all the province of Babylon, together with the freewill offering of the people and the priests, who offer willingly for the house of their God that is in Jerusalem.
verses.7:17: Therefore, with this money you shall diligently buy bulls, rams, and lambs, with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and you shall offer them upon the altar of the house of your God that is in Jerusalem.
verses.7:18: And whatever seems good to you and to your brethren to do with the rest of the silver and the gold, do according to the will of your God.
verses.7:19: Also the vessels that are given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver in full before the God of Jerusalem.
verses.7:20: And whatever else may be needed for the house of your God, which you may have occasion to supply, you shall pay from the king's treasury.
verses.7:21: And I, even I, King Artaxerxes, issue a decree to all the treasurers who are in the region beyond the River, that whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, requires of you, let it be done with all diligence,
verses.7:22: up to one hundred talents of silver, one hundred kors of wheat, one hundred baths of wine, one hundred baths of oil, and salt without prescribed limit.
verses.7:23: Whatever is commanded by the God of heaven, let it be done thoroughly for the house of the God of heaven; for why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons?
verses.7:24: Also we notify you that it shall not be lawful to impose tribute, custom, or toll upon any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nethinim, or servants of this house of God.
verses.7:25: And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges who may judge all the people who are in the region beyond the River, all who know the laws of your God; and those who do not know them, you shall teach.
verses.7:26: And whoever will not observe the law of your God and the law of the king, let judgment be strictly executed upon him, whether for death, or for banishment, or for confiscation of goods, or for imprisonment."
verses.7:27: Blessed be the LORD God of our fathers, who has put such a thing as this into the heart of the king, to adorn the house of the LORD that is in Jerusalem,
verses.7:28: and has extended lovingkindness to me before the king and his counselors, and before all the mighty princes of the king. So I took courage, as the hand of the LORD my God was upon me; and I gathered leading men from Israel to go up with me.
verses.8:1: Now these are the heads of their fathers' houses, and their genealogical enrollment—those who went up with me from Babylon in the reign of King Artaxerxes:
verses.8:2: Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of the sons of David, Hattush;
verses.8:3: Of the sons of Shecaniah, of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah; and with him were registered by genealogy one hundred and fifty males;
verses.8:4: Of the sons of Pahath-Moab, Eliehoenai the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males;
verses.8:5: Of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred males;
verses.8:6: And of the sons of Adin, Ebed the son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males;
verses.8:7: And of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah, and with him seventy males;
verses.8:8: And of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah the son of Michael, and with him eighty males;
verses.8:9: Of the sons of Joab, Obadiah the son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen males;
verses.8:10: And of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred and sixty males;
verses.8:11: And of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah the son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight males;
verses.8:12: And of the sons of Azgad, Johanan the son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred and ten males;
verses.8:13: And of the sons of Adonikam, the last ones—these were their names: Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah—and with them sixty males;
verses.8:14: And of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with him seventy males.
verses.8:15: Now I gathered them by the river that flows to Ahava, and we encamped there three days. And I looked closely among the people and the priests, and I found none of the sons of Levi there.
verses.8:16: Then I sent for Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, leading men; also for Joiarib and Elnathan, men of understanding.
verses.8:17: And I gave them a command for Iddo the chief man at the place Casiphia, and I put words in their mouths to speak to Iddo and his brother, the Nethinim, at the place Casiphia, that they should bring us ministers for the house of our God.
verses.8:18: Then, according to the good hand of our God upon us, they brought us a man of discretion from the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel, namely Sherebiah, with his sons and his brethren, eighteen;
verses.8:19: and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, his brethren and their sons, twenty;
verses.8:20: and of the Nethinim, whom David and the leaders had appointed for the service of the Levites, two hundred and twenty Nethinim. All of them were designated by name.
verses.8:21: Then I proclaimed a fast there at the river Ahava, that we might humble ourselves before our God, to seek from Him the right way for us and for our little ones and for all our possessions.
verses.8:22: For I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy along the way, because we had spoken to the king, saying, "The hand of our God is upon all who seek Him for good, but His power and His wrath are against all who forsake Him."
verses.8:23: So we fasted and petitioned our God concerning this, and He heard our plea.
verses.8:24: And I set apart twelve of the leaders of the priests, along with Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brethren with them,
verses.8:25: and weighed out to them the silver, the gold, and the vessels—the offering for the house of our God which the king and his counselors and his officials, and all Israel who were present, had offered.
verses.8:26: Thus I weighed into their hand six hundred and fifty talents of silver, and silver vessels weighing one hundred talents, and one hundred talents of gold,
verses.8:27: also twenty gold bowls worth one thousand darics, and two vessels of fine polished bronze, precious as gold.
verses.8:28: And I said to them, "You are holy to the LORD, and the vessels are holy; and the silver and the gold are a freewill offering to the LORD God of your fathers.
verses.8:29: Watch and keep them until you weigh them out before the leaders of the priests and the Levites and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel in Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of the LORD."
verses.8:30: So the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and the gold and the vessels, to bring them to Jerusalem to the house of our God.
verses.8:31: Then we departed from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month to go to Jerusalem. And the hand of our God was upon us, and He delivered us from the hand of the enemy and from those who lay in ambush along the way.
verses.8:32: So we came to Jerusalem, and remained there three days.
verses.8:33: Now on the fourth day the silver and the gold and the vessels were weighed in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest, and with him was Eleazar the son of Phinehas; and with them were Jozabad the son of Jeshua and Noadiah the son of Binnui, the Levites.
verses.8:34: Everything was accounted for by number and by weight, and the entire weight was recorded at that time.
verses.8:35: Those who had come from captivity, the sons of the exile, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All this was a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.8:36: And they delivered the king's decrees to the king's satraps and to the governors beyond the River; and they supported the people and the house of God.
verses.9:1: When these things were finished, the leaders approached me, saying, "The people of Israel and the priests and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, concerning their abominations—those of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
verses.9:2: For they have taken some of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, so that the holy seed has mingled with the peoples of the lands. Indeed, the hand of the leaders and the rulers has been foremost in this unfaithfulness."
verses.9:3: And when I heard this matter, I tore my garment and my robe, and plucked out some of the hair of my head and my beard, and sat down appalled.
verses.9:4: Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel assembled to me because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles, while I sat appalled until the evening offering.
verses.9:5: And at the evening offering I arose from my fasting, with my garment and my robe torn, and I bowed down on my knees and spread out my hands to the LORD my God.
verses.9:6: And I said, "O my God, I am ashamed and humiliated to lift up my face to You, my God; for our iniquities have risen higher than our heads, and our guilt has grown up to the heavens.
verses.9:7: From the days of our fathers to this day we have been in great guilt; and because of our iniquities we, our kings, and our priests have been delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to shame of face, as it is this day.
verses.9:8: And now for a brief moment favor has been shown by the LORD our God, to leave us a remnant to escape and to give us a peg in His holy place, that our God may enlighten our eyes and grant us a measure of revival in our bondage.
verses.9:9: For we are bondservants; yet our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but He has extended lovingkindness to us in the sight of the kings of Persia, to grant us revival, to raise up the house of our God, to repair its ruins, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
verses.9:10: And now, O our God, what shall we say after this? For we have forsaken Your commandments,
verses.9:11: which You commanded by Your servants the prophets, saying, 'The land which you are entering to possess is an unclean land, defiled by the uncleanness of the peoples of the lands, by their abominations with which they have filled it from one end to the other in their impurity.
verses.9:12: Now therefore, do not give your daughters to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons; and never seek their peace or their prosperity, that you may be strong and eat the good of the land, and leave it as an inheritance to your children forever.'
verses.9:13: And after all that has come upon us for our evil deeds and for our great guilt, since You our God have punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and have given us such a remnant as this,
verses.9:14: should we again break Your commandments, and join in marriage with the peoples of these abominations? Would You not be angry with us until You had consumed us, so that there would be neither remnant nor survivor?
verses.9:15: O LORD God of Israel, You are righteous, for we are left as a remnant that has escaped, as it is this day. Behold, we are before You in our guilt, for no one can stand before You because of this."
verses.10:1: Now as Ezra prayed and made confession, weeping and prostrating himself before the house of God, a very great congregation from Israel assembled to him—men, women, and children—for the people wept with great weeping.
verses.10:2: And Shechaniah the son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, answered and said to Ezra, "We have acted unfaithfully against our God and have taken foreign wives from the peoples of the land; yet now there is hope in Israel concerning this matter.
verses.10:3: Now therefore, let us make a covenant with our God to put away all the wives and those born of them, according to the counsel of the Lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God; and let it be done according to the law.
verses.10:4: Arise, for this matter belongs to you, and we are with you. Be strong and act!"
verses.10:5: Then Ezra arose and made the leaders of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear an oath to act according to this word. And they swore.
verses.10:6: Then Ezra rose from before the house of God and went into the chamber of Jehohanan the son of Eliashib; and when he went there, he ate no bread and drank no water, for he mourned over the unfaithfulness of those of the captivity.
verses.10:7: And they issued a proclamation throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the sons of the captivity, to gather together at Jerusalem,
verses.10:8: and that whoever did not come within three days, according to the counsel of the leaders and the elders, all his property should be forfeited, and he himself separated from the assembly of the captivity.
verses.10:9: So all the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled at Jerusalem within the three days. It was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month; and all the people sat in the open square of the house of God, trembling on account of the matter and because of the heavy rains.
verses.10:10: Then Ezra the priest arose and said to them, "You have acted unfaithfully and have taken foreign wives, adding to the guilt of Israel.
verses.10:11: Now therefore, make confession to the LORD God of your fathers and do His will; separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign wives."
verses.10:12: Then all the congregation answered and said with a loud voice, "Yes! According to your word it is our duty to do.
verses.10:13: Yet the people are many, and it is the season of heavy rains, and there is no strength to stand outside; nor is this a work of one day or two, for we have greatly transgressed in this matter.
verses.10:14: Let our leaders stand for the entire congregation, and let all in our cities who have taken foreign wives come at appointed times, together with the elders of every city and its judges, until the fierce wrath of our God is turned away from us concerning this matter."
verses.10:15: Only Jonathan the son of Asahel and Jahaziah the son of Tikvah stood against this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supported them.
verses.10:16: So the sons of the captivity did thus. And Ezra the priest, together with men who were heads of the fathers' houses according to their fathers' houses, all of them designated by name, were set apart; and they sat down on the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.
verses.10:17: By the first day of the first month they had finished with all the men who had taken foreign wives.
verses.10:18: Now among the sons of the priests who had taken foreign wives were found, of the sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brethren: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
verses.10:19: And they gave their pledge to put away their wives; and being guilty, they presented a ram of the flock for their guilt.
verses.10:20: And of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
verses.10:21: And of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
verses.10:22: And of the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
verses.10:23: And of the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah—that is, Kelita—Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
verses.10:24: And of the singers: Eliashib. And of the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
verses.10:25: And of Israel, of the sons of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
verses.10:26: And of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
verses.10:27: And of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
verses.10:28: And of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
verses.10:29: And of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Ramoth.
verses.10:30: And of the sons of Pahath-Moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
verses.10:31: And of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
verses.10:33: Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
verses.10:34: Of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel,
verses.10:43: Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.
verses.10:44: All these had taken foreign wives, and some of them had wives by whom they had children.

notes.1:1: The phrase "sent a proclamation" translates a Hebrew idiom meaning "caused a voice to pass through." Jeremiah had prophesied that Judah's captivity in Babylon would last seventy years (Jeremiah 25:11-12; 29:10).
notes.1:6: The expression "strengthened their hands" is a Hebrew idiom for lending practical assistance and encouragement, echoing the decree in verse 4 to support the returning exiles.
notes.1:9: The Hebrew nouns translated "basins" and "knives" occur only here in the Hebrew Bible, making their exact identification uncertain.
notes.1:11: The Masoretic total of five thousand four hundred is larger than the sum of the items enumerated in verses 9 and 10, likely because those earlier verses list only the principal vessels.
notes.2:1: The Masoretic ketiv writes the king's name with an extra vav as Nebuchadnezzor, while the traditional qere followed here reads Nebuchadnezzar. The phrase "the province" refers to the Persian administrative district of Judah.
notes.2:6: Pahath-Moab means "governor of Moab" and served as the ancestral name of a prominent Judean clan, here reckoned through its branches of Jeshua and Joab.
notes.2:25: Kiriath Arim is a shortened Masoretic spelling of Kiriath Jearim (compare Nehemiah 7:29), listed together with the neighboring towns of Chephirah and Beeroth.
notes.2:31: "The other Elam" distinguishes this clan or settlement from the Elam recorded earlier in verse 7, though both entries share the exact same total.
notes.2:43: The Hebrew term Nethinim literally means "those given," designating hereditary temple servants appointed to assist the Levites in sanctuary duties.
notes.2:46: Following the Masoretic qere Shalmai (compare Nehemiah 7:48); the ketiv transposes the middle consonants to read Shamlai.
notes.2:50: Following the Masoretic qere Nephusim; the ketiv reads Nephisim.
notes.2:63: The Hebrew title Tirshatha is an Old Persian honorific for the provincial governor. Urim and Thummim were the sacred objects kept in the high priest's breastpiece to discern the LORD's will.
notes.3:3: The traditional reading (Qere) has the plural verb 'they offered,' whereas the written consonantal text (Ketiv) has the singular 'he offered.'
notes.3:10: Literally 'by the hands of David,' an idiom denoting liturgical directions established by King David.
notes.4:2: The Qere reads 'to Him' (we have been sacrificing), while the Ketiv reads 'not,' which would imply they had not sacrificed since Esarhaddon's time.
notes.4:4: The Qere corrects an orthographic transposition in the Ketiv without altering the meaning 'frightening' or 'troubling.'
notes.4:8: From this verse through Ezra 6:18 the original text shifts from Hebrew into Biblical Aramaic, the official administrative language of the Persian Empire.
notes.4:9: The Qere supplies the emphatic plural gentilic forms rendered 'Archevites' and 'Dehaites,' where the Ketiv writes shorter consonantal forms (the latter sometimes read as 'Dehavites').
notes.4:12: The Qere supplies the emphatic plural 'the walls' and standard Aramaic verb form 'finishing' for the shorter or variant spellings of the Ketiv.
notes.5:4: The Aramaic text literally uses the first-person plural 'we told them,' reflecting either the Jewish builders' response to the Persian officials or an echo of the officials' own first-person inquiry recorded in verses 9-10.
notes.5:8: Literally 'stones of rolling,' referring to massive hewn blocks moved into place on rollers.
notes.5:15: The Qere reads the shorter Aramaic demonstrative 'these' where the Ketiv writes the longer form; the meaning is identical.
notes.6:2: Aramaic Achmetha, the royal summer capital of Media known in Greek as Ecbatana.
notes.6:6: The Aramaic term apharsekaye, traditionally transliterated Apharsachites, is likely a Persian administrative title meaning investigators or officials.
notes.6:14: Following the qere neviyya, meaning the prophet, which represents standard Aramaic orthography for the ketiv neviyah.
notes.6:17: Following the qere lechattaah, meaning as a sin offering; the ketiv reflects an alternate spelling or plural form.
notes.6:22: Here the king of Assyria refers to Darius, the Persian monarch whose empire absorbed and ruled the former Assyrian territory.
notes.7:7: The Nethinim, literally the given ones, were dedicated temple servants assigned to assist the Levites in sanctuary duties.
notes.7:12: The Aramaic closing of the salutation is an abbreviated imperial chancery greeting meaning complete peace and now; the adjective may alternatively describe Ezra as an accomplished scribe.
notes.7:18: Following the qere forms for to you and your brethren, which standardize the Aramaic suffix orthography against the plene spellings of the ketiv.
notes.7:25: Following the qere participle meaning judging; the ketiv is an older orthographic variant with the same meaning.
notes.7:26: Following the qere lishroshi, meaning for banishment or uprooting; the ketiv reflects an alternate abstract noun ending.
notes.8:14: The Hebrew Ketiv reads "and Zabbud," while the Qere followed here reads "and Zaccur."
notes.8:17: The Qere reads "I gave them a command" where the Ketiv has "I sent them out," and reads "the Nethinim" (hereditary temple servants, cf. 8:20) where the Ketiv writes a slightly fuller spelling.
notes.8:24: Sherebiah and Hashabiah were Levites (8:18-19); Ezra sets apart twelve leading priests together with these two Levites and ten of their brethren, forming two groups of twelve (cf. 8:30).
notes.8:25: The Ketiv and Qere differ only in the spelling of the verb "I weighed out." In 8:27, the "daric" was a standard Persian gold coin.
notes.9:8: Literally "a peg" (tent peg or nail), a biblical image of secure foothold and stability granted by God in His sanctuary.
notes.9:11: Literally "from mouth to mouth," a Hebrew idiom denoting complete extent from one end to the other.
notes.9:13: Literally "You have held back downward from our iniquity," an idiom expressing that God's discipline was far lighter than Israel's sin merited.
notes.10:2: Following the Hebrew qere, Elam (matching Ezra 2:7 and 10:26); the ketiv reads Olam.
notes.10:3: The Masoretic text reads the Lord (Adonai); some interpreters read the consonants without the Masoretic vocalization as my lord, referring to Ezra.
notes.10:12: Following the Hebrew qere, singular your word; the ketiv reads plural your words.
notes.10:29: Following the Hebrew qere, Ramoth (ketiv Jeremoth); likewise the qere is followed in verses 35 (Cheluhu), 37 (Jaasai), and 43 (Jaddai).
notes.10:44: Following the Hebrew qere, had taken; the closing clause is terse in the Masoretic text, literally stating that among them were wives and they produced children.
